column1: #mapping_set_title: HELO cross-ontology relationships and mappings to the Curriculum KG Ontology and schema.org

#mapping_set_description: Two tiers. Primary rows (mapping_tier primary) are exactly the cross-ontology annotation assertions of helo.ttl and helo-pathways.ttl, each reified there as an axiom with its linking kind and its reason, and each row's comment is that reason word for word. They are helo:9000006 proposed to prepare for task (pathway to HETO task specification), helo:9000008 has corresponding HETO role, helo:9000014 is derived from HEO property and helo:9000013 uses ontology, with predicate_type owl annotation property. Secondary rows are in this file only. They map HELO classes and properties to the Curriculum KG Ontology (Christou et al. 2025) and to schema.org with SKOS predicates read from the HELO subject. A broad match says the object is broader than the HELO subject and a narrow match that it is narrower, and the build checks each broad reason says broader. No row states identity and none uses skos:exactMatch. Every row carries one of the five linking kinds as the CURIE of a HEAO 0.2.0 individual. Convention. A relationship from a HELO record to a HETO role or a HEO relationship type describes or records that thing and is representational. Preparing a learner for a HETO task and a module using an ontology are typed representational as the nearest of the five kinds, since none fits exactly, and HEAO is asked whether a preparatory or instructional kind is wanted. Mappings describe meaning and are definitional. HELO's relationships from steps, goals and pathways to HEO concepts are instance data typed representational on the property itself and are not rows of this file. No HEO concept about learning, curricula or the semantic layer exists in HEO 2.0.0, so no row maps a HELO term to HEO. heont:helo names the core file and heont:helo/helo-pathways.owl the pathway file. The uses ontology rows read the outline literally and point at each ontology, not at a version, so their object_source_version is empty. Modules 2 and 5 use HEO concept addresses and the wiki's graph, but their outline rows do not name an ontology, so they have no uses ontology row.

#comment: Written by src/build_helo.py and drafted by Michelle Ashley with Claude. Every row is proposed and unreviewed, so mapping_justification is semapv:UnspecifiedMatching. Signing rows off is for the curators, Michelle Ashley and Darrin Baines, later. A signed row becomes semapv:ManualMappingCuration with reviewer_id, and rejected rows are removed. Confidence is a house scale fixed by kind, 0.9 for a curated primary row or a close match, 0.8 for a broad or narrow match, 0.7 for a related match and 0.6 for a primary row made by a rule (the 15 task preparation rows, whose share of covered concepts is on their axiom), not a measured confidence. The Curriculum KG IRIs did not resolve on 19 October 2026 (they redirect to kastle-lab.github.io/education-gateway and give 404). Its schema is readable at https://kastle-lab.github.io/curriculum-kg/ontology.ttl with the same SHA-256 as commit cfd55d372ce5190e05a79498db3204c4b14f914f, it declares no version IRI, so object_source_version is empty, and its sample data and competency questions use https://edugate.cs.wright.edu/lod/ontology/ without currKG, so these rows do not join to its instance data without a rewrite. schema.org was read at release V30.1.

The HELO profile health economist describes people who bear this HETO role. HELO defines health economist as "An intended learner profile of a person who works in health economics, in research, in practice or in government." and HETO defines health economics practitioner role as "A role borne by a person that is realised when that person carries out health economics work, such as framing, costing, modelling, analysing or reporting an economic evaluation.". The profile is information about an audience and the role is borne by people, so the profile describes the role's bearers, a representational relationship.

The HELO profile economic modeller describes people who bear this HETO role. HELO defines economic modeller as "An intended learner profile of a person who designs, builds, runs or checks economic models." and HETO defines economic modeller role as "A health economics practitioner role that is realised when its bearer designs, builds, runs or checks an economic model.". The profile is information about an audience and the role is borne by people, so the profile describes the role's bearers, a representational relationship.

The site publishes each pathway as a schema.org ItemList of its steps in ascending order. An item list is any list of items, ordered or not, so it is broader. schema.org V30.1 of 16 September 2026, read on 2026-10-19, described in HELO's own words.

Each is a sequence of learning steps in order. In Curriculum KG each persona determines exactly one learning path and a path is scoped by a curriculum, while a HELO pathway follows one subdomain, may be meant for several profiles and need not belong to a curriculum. Not a parent class, because Curriculum KG requires every learning step to have exactly one next and one previous step, which the first and last steps of a pathway lack. Curriculum KG Ontology (Christou et al. 2025), docs/ontology.ttl at commit cfd55d3, readable at https://kastle-lab.github.io/curriculum-kg/ontology.ttl, read on 2026-10-19. Its comments are described in HELO's own words with attribution, because the ontology is licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

The site publishes each step as a schema.org ListItem with its position. A list item is any entry in a list, so it is broader. schema.org V30.1 of 16 September 2026, read on 2026-10-19, described in HELO's own words.

Each is one ordered place in a learning path. A Curriculum KG step points to exactly one module, while a HELO step names one learning topic and its core and optional HEO concepts and points to no module. Curriculum KG Ontology (Christou et al. 2025), docs/ontology.ttl at commit cfd55d3, readable at https://kastle-lab.github.io/curriculum-kg/ontology.ttl, read on 2026-10-19. Its comments are described in HELO's own words with attribution, because the ontology is licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

Each names a subject that learning content is about. Curriculum KG requires every topic to have both a broader and a narrower topic, which no finite set of topics can meet, while HELO leaves topic hierarchy to HEO and the Knowledge Tree. Curriculum KG Ontology (Christou et al. 2025), docs/ontology.ttl at commit cfd55d3, readable at https://kastle-lab.github.io/curriculum-kg/ontology.ttl, read on 2026-10-19. Its comments are described in HELO's own words with attribution, because the ontology is licensed CC BY-SA 4.0.

Each profiles an audience by role or background. A Curriculum KG persona determines exactly one learning path, while a HELO profile may be meant for several pathways and curricula. Curriculum KG Ontology (Christou et al. 2025), docs/ontology.ttl at commit cfd55d3, readable at https://kastle-lab.github.io/curriculum-kg/ontology.ttl, read on 2026-10-19. A schema.org Audience is the intended group for whom an item was created, which matches an intended learner profile. schema.org V30.1 of 16 September 2026, read on 2026-10-19, described in HELO's own words.

Each gathers modules into one course of study offered as a whole. A schema.org Course describes an educational course that may run as several instances, which matches a HELO curriculum. HELO does not model course instances. schema.org V30.1 of 16 September 2026, read on 2026-10-19, described in HELO's own words.

Each is a unit of content inside a curriculum, about one or more topics. Curriculum KG also asks every module for a category, a level and referenced media, which HELO does not. schema.org competencyRequired names knowledge, skill or another attribute needed before a resource can be understood, and is in schema.org's new area, so it may change. HELO builds on concept names HEO concepts that a pathway builds on, and the two have different ranges, so they are related only. schema.org V30.1 of 16 September 2026, read on 2026-10-19, described in HELO's own words.

schema.org teaches names a competency or learning outcome that a resource helps a person learn. A HELO learning goal is a separate objective record, and for a pathway it names concepts to understand, not a competency. schema.org V30.1 of 16 September 2026, read on 2026-10-19, described in HELO's own words.
